affordance_in_statement: The first line provides two integers k and t ($1 \le k \le 22$, $0 \le t \le k^3$), representing the quantity of each resource type and the total number of certified triplets.
removal_suggestion: Because the numerical bound is immutable, re-present it through the scenario rather than as an isolated small-limit hint, and explicitly state that test registries may be dense and adversarially ordered; this discourages assuming that constrained-first backtracking will terminate quickly.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The explicit resource IDs from 1 to k and the small bound k <= 22 make specialist, machine, and time usage naturally representable as bitmasks.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses recursive backtracking with pruning and bitmasks to search for a perfect 3-dimensional matching.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The small common domain size k <= 22 and explicit certified-triplet registry support direct subset-search state representations.

common_affordance: The immutable small domain bound k <= 22 makes exponential bitmask/backtracking search appear practical.

Its general backtracking search has exponential worst-case behavior and timed out on a hard instance.
